## The Problem

**MSTest.Sdk v4 dropped VSTest support by default.** Starting with v4, `MSTest.Sdk` sets `TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport=true` and only enables Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP). The VSTest adapter is no longer included, so `vstest.console` finds zero tests.

## Your Options

### Option 1: Re-enable VSTest compatibility (quick CI fix)

Add this property to your `.csproj`:

```xml
<EnableMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunnerForVSTest>true</EnableMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunnerForVSTest>
```

This ships a VSTest adapter bridge so `vstest.console` can still discover tests.

### Option 2 (Recommended): Migrate your CI to use `dotnet test`

Since your project already uses MTP, switch your CI from `vstest.console` to:

```bash
dotnet test TestProject.csproj
```

This is the intended path forward with MSTest.Sdk v4.

So the error fires when:
1. `IsTestingPlatformApplication` is true (set by MSTest.Sdk v4)
2. `TargetFramework` is not empty
3. `_SupportsGlobalJsonTestRunner` is true (SDK >= 10)

The condition checks if it's a VSTest target being used. This is the `_GetTestsProject` target which is the VSTest target invoked by `dotnet test` in old mode. On .NET 10+, `dotnet test` uses a new protocol.

The fix is in `global.json` - on .NET 10+ SDK, `dotnet test` needs to be configured to use the new test runner protocol. 

I need to figure out what configuration goes into `global.json` to enable the new test runner on SDK 10+.
